steps: Here worker A takes ticket T one thousand and one, a twenty step task: classify, research the knowledge base, fix, and verify. Step one comes back as technical, authentication.
Workers crash mid-task. With state held only in memory, dying at step fifteen means starting again from step one, losing fourteen steps.
So now, after every step, you save the step number, the messages and metadata to shared storage as a checkpoint.
Steps two to fourteen repeat the same beat: ask Claude, read the result, and save the checkpoint.
Then worker A crashes at step fifteen. This time the loss is just one step, not fourteen.
Next, a fresh, stateless worker B boots and loads the checkpoint from shared storage, the state after step fourteen, so it resumes at step fifteen.
Finally, worker B re-runs step fifteen, which is safe because each step is idempotent, and ticket T one thousand and one carries on.
